body:
`lockdown.command` returns a `run`/`build` command's output as the program wrote it. Cargo's own replies already go through `diagnostics.strip_ansi`, but named commands don't. In run 9d47034f122fa14c of task:56ecdeaa0356d0db, `run cargo-fmt-check` returned a long rustfmt diff where every changed line was wrapped in terminal colour codes (`\u001b[31m … \u001b(B\u001b[m`). That roughly doubled the size of a reply that was already large, and it came right before the agent's context was compacted.

Change: pass the output of `lockdown.command` through `diagnostics.strip_ansi` before `condense` and `trim_output`, so the size budget is spent on text the agent can read.

Check: a test where a command prints ANSI-coloured lines, and the reply contains the plain text with no escape sequences.

2 questions before proceeding: What's the true scope of this and similar waste-trimming actions? And is this a safe change that won't have negative unforeseen consequences?
title: run: strip colour codes from command output
